about.title: Seaside Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often in the time it takes to walk through a grocery store entrance on Broadway Avenue or a rain-slicked parking lot near Noche Buena Street. In Monterey County, property owners and businesses have a legal duty to keep their spaces reasonably safe, but proving they knew about a hazard and didn't fix it takes more than a photo on your phone. Wet floors, broken pavement, poor lighting, and unmarked steps are common triggers for these claims across Seaside's retail corridors and residential complexes. Because California law requires you to show the owner had notice of the danger, timing and evidence matter enormously — surveillance footage often gets erased within days or weeks. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in the area who can evaluate what happened, gather the right records, and explain your options before your two-year window closes.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Seaside Premises Liability Claim

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help identify maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish this.

items.title: Video Doesn't Last Forever
items.desc: Many Seaside businesses overwrite surveillance footage within days. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make the difference in a notice-based claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Still Allows Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the fall — your share of fault simply reduces the final recovery rather than barring it.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Seaside?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government-owned property in Monterey County was involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early formal claim. An independent attorney can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Fremont Boulevard or Del Monte Boulevard and didn't take photos?
items.answer: Photos help, but they're not the only evidence available. Incident reports, witness statements, and store surveillance video can often reconstruct what happened even without your own pictures. An attorney can send a preservation request to the business quickly to try to secure that footage before it's deleted.

items.question: Do I need to prove the property owner was negligent on purpose?
items.answer: No, California premises liability law doesn't require intent. You generally need to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazardous condition and didn't fix it or warn visitors within a reasonable time. This is often the central issue an attorney will investigate.
